beats.say: The first minutes matter most. The attacker is in a hurry, so you need to be faster.
Stop when something looks wrong: a sign-in you do not know, a window that opens itself, missing files.

body.text: Someone signed in to your account from

beats.say: In an emergency, call technical support or the security team. The email can wait until later.
If you suspect the computer, do not report from it. The attacker may read the mail, so phone instead.

scenes.title: A strange morning
scenes.intro: You start your computer in the morning and notice a few strange things. How do you react to each?

body.text: Someone signed in to your account from Ganja on an unknown device at 03:12.

steps.say: If this sign-in was not you, what do you do?

actions.label: It was not me: report
actions.feedback: Correct, an unknown sign-in means someone has your password. Reporting fast saves the account.

actions.label: Dismiss
actions.feedback: The attacker is still in your account and gaining time. Report a notice like this at once.

body.text: An operator wants to see your screen and control your computer.

actions.label: Decline
actions.feedback: Correct, you did not ask for support. Report an unexpected request like this too.

actions.label: Allow
actions.feedback: The remote person now controls your computer. Never allow support you did not call yourself.

actions.label: Decline and report
actions.feedback: Excellent. An unexpected remote access request must be reported at once.

body.text: Pay within 72 hours to get your files back. If you switch off the computer, the files will be deleted.

steps.say: A ransom demand is on screen. Your first step?

actions.label: Unplug the cable, turn off Wi-Fi
actions.feedback: Correct, going offline stops the spread. Leave the computer on and call at once.

actions.label: Switch off the computer
actions.feedback: Switching off can erase traces in memory. Unless your procedure says otherwise, go offline and leave it on.

actions.label: Open the payment page
actions.feedback: Paying does not guarantee your files back. Never pay, leave the decision to specialists.

body.text: Not urgent: the Report button or security@idare.example

actions.label: Call now
actions.feedback: Correct. Report an urgent incident by phone: the specialist tells you what to do right away.

actions.label: Email tomorrow
actions.feedback: Encryption spreads and every minute counts. This mailbox may not be safe any more either.

question.prompt: A stranger signed in to your account. Who do you tell?

options.label: Technical support or the security team
options.feedback: Correct. Only they can lock and check the account.

options.label: My manager as well
options.feedback: Correct. Your manager helps organise the work but does not replace the specialist.

options.label: Only colleagues in my department
options.feedback: Colleagues cannot lock the account, so time is lost.

options.label: I post it on social media so everyone knows
options.feedback: Posting about an incident helps the attacker and other scammers.

scenes.explain: The specialist fixes it, your manager is informed, nobody else is needed.

scenes.prompt: Pick the way to report each situation.

pairs.right: Send it with the Report button

pairs.left: A ransom demand is on screen

pairs.right: Call at once so they can lock it remotely

pairs.left: A file went to the wrong person
pairs.right: Tell your manager and the security team

scenes.explain: For urgent or spreading cases, phone. Report the rest with the Report button or by email.

nodes.text: Do not worry, it is probably an update. Do not make a fuss.
nodes.speaker: Tural (colleague), looking at the strange window
nodes.spoken: Do not worry, uh, it is probably an update. Do not make a fuss.

choices.label: I still call technical support
choices.feedback: Correct. A false alarm is no problem, a late report is.

choices.label: I wait, maybe it goes away
choices.feedback: Waiting gives the attacker time. If in doubt, call.

nodes.text: What did you see and what did you do?
nodes.speaker: Technical support
nodes.spoken: What did you see <short pause> and what did you do?

choices.label: I keep it short: what, when, which computer, what I did
choices.feedback: Excellent. With exact details the specialist can start right away.

choices.label: I closed the window, I do not remember
choices.feedback: Every detail helps. Next time take a photo of the screen with your phone.

points: When something looks wrong, stop and report at once.
In an emergency, phone. Do not report from a suspect computer.
A false alarm is fine, a delay is dangerous.
